package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of 'tar' and '@npmcli/arborist' contain ZIP slip vulnerabilities that allow attackers to craft malicious npm packages which, when installed or extracted, can overwrite arbitrary files on the filesystem. This can lead to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running npm install, even if lifecycle scripts are disabled.

execution_context.file_location: npm package archive (.tar.gz/.tgz) with malicious file paths

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: archive contains file entries with paths like '../../../../../etc/passwd' or './.npmrc'
malicious_snippets.code_language: archive file structure (not code, but malicious path entries)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the vulnerable tar/arborist package extracts the archive, it does not properly sanitize file paths, allowing files to be written outside the intended directory (directory traversal). This can overwrite sensitive files or place malicious files in privileged locations.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of directory traversal sequences (../) in archive file paths is a classic indicator of an attempt to escape the intended extraction directory and overwrite arbitrary files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal extraction tools should sanitize and prevent writing files outside the target directory. The vulnerable packages fail to do so, violating this security expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate archives should never contain directory traversal in file paths. Only backup/restore tools with explicit user consent might use such paths.
key_indicators: Presence of '../' or absolute paths in archive entries
Extraction results in files being written outside the target directory
Overwriting of sensitive files (e.g., .npmrc, .bashrc, system files)

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious npm package archive with file entries containing directory traversal sequences (e.g., '../../etc/passwd').
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious archive is published to npm or delivered to the victim.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the malicious npm package using npm CLI, which uses the vulnerable tar/arborist package to extract the archive.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction process writes files outside the intended directory, potentially overwriting sensitive files.

attack_chain.action: Overwritten files may contain attacker-controlled content, leading to arbitrary code execution or configuration compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution or escalates privileges on the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction resulting in files being written outside the intended directory
Presence of '../' or absolute paths in archive file entries
Unexpected overwriting of sensitive files during npm install
file_indicators: npm package archives (.tar.gz/.tgz) with directory traversal in file paths
Overwritten .npmrc, .bashrc, or system files after npm install
network_indicators: No direct network indicators (attack is local to extraction process)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package archives for file entries containing '../' or absolute paths. During npm install or tar extraction, alert if files are written outside the target directory or if sensitive files are unexpectedly modified. Use file integrity monitoring on critical files to detect unauthorized changes after package installation.
